title: After-action lab: rollout synthesis and rollback safety hardening
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: During a controlled canary of model v4.2.0 we observed a correlated surge in repeated-token rates and 5xx spike at ~15% traffic. Shadow vs live comparison showed divergence in KV-cache hit patterns and an autoscaler-induced pod churn that exposed a race in cache warming. This ticket captures the after-action lab, proposed permanent mitigations, runbook edits, and automation to reduce human-in-the-loop rollback time.

Key findings:
- Root cause hypothesis: KV-cache warmup race combined with short-lived scale-up events caused inconsistent cache priming. When the new model was receiving traffic in canary, early requests experienced lower KV hits leading to higher generation instability (repetition) and CPU pressure that crossed an internal error threshold.
- Signal gap: our staged-release dashboards tracked 5xx rate and avg latency but did not expose per-model KV-hit ratio or per-pod cold-start token-loss metric; shadow traffic telemetry was sampled at 0.5% which under-sampled edge cases.
- Canary policy weaknesses: canary window was 20 minutes with traffic ramp at 1%, 5%, 15% — this allowed enough time for autoscaler to trigger because of bursty synthetic test traffic, accelerating exposure before stable warmup.

Decisions and trade-offs taken in lab:
- Increase canary steady window to 45 minutes for large model changes (>= 5% architecture change) to allow cache stabilization. Trade-off: longer rollout duration vs fewer false positives and safer rollouts.
- Require explicit KV-warmup synthetic stage in the rollout pipeline before ramping traffic beyond 5%. This adds cost (short synthetic traffic burst) but avoids repeated-token customer impact.
- Tighten circuit-breaker to detect token-repetition surges (custom metric) and trigger auto-rollback at a lower threshold than generic 5xx-only rules. We accept potential more frequent rollbacks for safety.

Runbook updates (items to add):
1) Pre-rollout: run KV-warmup job (script: tools/warmup/kv_warmup.py) and verify per-pod kv_hit_ratio >= 0.85 in Prometheus for 5 consecutive minutes.
2) Canary stages: add explicit "shadow-validation" stage at 1% traffic for 15 minutes with 5% shadow sampling and run automated quality checks (repetition-rate, perplexity-proxy, latency p95).
3) Auto-rollback conditions: if repetition-rate increases by >25% over baseline AND kv_hit_ratio < 0.7 on >=3 pods for 3 consecutive 1m buckets, initiate rollback.
4) Emergency operator script: rollout-abort.sh that performs immediate traffic re-route, starts diagnostic trace collection, and creates incident channel (#inc-rollouts).

Telemetry and observability roadmap items:
- Add per-model, per-pod kv_hit_ratio metric to the default rollout dashboard (dashboard link below).
- Increase shadow sampling on first canary to 5% for 30 minutes (configurable by PR).
- Add synthetic stress test in CI that simulates autoscaler behavior while warming cache to validate stability.

Automation tasks (epics/planned PRs):
- ENG-411224: Implement auto-rollback rule for repetition-rate metric and integrate with rollout sequencer.
- ENG-411225: Add KV-warmup stage to pipeline orchestration and UI flag in Console for forced warmup.
- ENG-411226: Extend shadow capture to include token-level diff diagnostic and store for 7 days.
